output:
**What I found:** Two of the three findings, the cent and the date, are bugs with a clear right answer that got past unit tests built to catch exactly that kind of logic. The button finding is a design question that needs a person to decide it. I rate the current test portfolio as not good enough, because it reported green while two checkable errors were live (the record calls this NOT-ADEQUATE). The persona agents are exploratory testing: they should run before promotion, not after merge to main, and they should never block a release.

**Why it matters:** If each finding is only fixed in place, the next rounding or timezone edge case will again be caught by an agent on a live environment, or by a customer. If the agents are made to block releases, the subjective findings turn into weak automated checks and the deployment pipeline gets slower without getting more reliable.

**Do this first:**
1. For the cent finding, get the rounding rule from the pricing owner. Is the discount rounded per line or on the order total? Half-up or half-even? Then add that rule as a regression example in the pricing unit tests. Without the rule there is no expected value to test against.
2. For the date finding, inject the clock and timezone into the delivery-date calculation and test the times around the cutoff (22:59, 23:00, 23:01, local midnight, and both DST switch days). Also add a smoke check on the assembled service that confirms which timezone it actually runs in.
3. File the Process/Submit finding as an issue for the UX owner, attaching the persona's evidence. Don't write a test for it.

**What I did not check:**
- Why the unit tests passed. This workspace has no product code or tests, only skill files. Open the existing pricing and delivery-date tests to see which of these it was: the rounding is done with floats, the test asserts the same wrong formula, the 23:00 boundary has no test case, or the tests pin the timezone to UTC.
- Whether "live environment" means production. If it does, the agents may be creating real orders. Check the agents' target URL and credentials.
- Whether Process and Submit both need to exist. Run `/functionality-complexity-tradeoff` on the two actions.

---

| Risk / criterion | Failure mode | Oracle | Technique | Scope / fidelity | Dependencies | Data / environment | Evidence | Residual blind spot |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Discounted order total | Total is 0.01 low after a percentage discount | Pricing owner's rounding rule (where it applies, which mode) checked against exact decimal arithmetic. **Rule not yet confirmed: DEFER until stated** | The escaped case as an example test, plus a property test: the discounted total equals the rule applied to exact decimals across generated line counts, prices and percentages | Pricing logic, in process (hermetic) | Real owned collaborators, no doubles | Generated cases; keep any minimal failing case found | None yet. The persona report is the only evidence | Whether display, invoice and payment amounts are rounded by the same code path |
| Delivery-date calculation | Order after 23:00 shows a delivery date one day early | The delivery-promise rule: cutoff time and which timezone counts as the order date. Confirm with the domain owner | Boundary values: 22:59/23:00/23:01, local midnight, both DST changes, an order placed on the day before a non-delivery day | Date logic, in process, with clock and timezone injected | Controlled clock, not a mock | Fixed timestamps per case | None yet | Whether the deployed runtime and database use the same timezone the tests assume |
| Timezone in the running system | Server or database runs in UTC while the business rule uses local time | The configured timezone matches the business timezone; one known order placed at 23:30 local gets the expected date | Real-environment integration / smoke check | Assembled service on a preview environment | Real runtime and real database | One synthetic order | None | Managed services whose timezone differs from staging |
| Process vs Submit distinguishability | People can't tell what each button does | No automated oracle. Needs the UX owner's judgment; testing with real users if they want evidence | Usability evaluation, if the owner asks for it | Not a test | n/a | n/a | Persona report only. The agent's claim about what users can't tell apart is a hypothesis, not observed user behaviour | Accessibility of the labels (descriptive labels, consistent identification): send to an accessibility specialist |

```text
Subject:              Post-merge persona-agent evaluation and the three escaped findings
Mode:                 Audit
Strategy pass:        Combined (current architecture treated as stable; not inspected)
Decision:             NOT-ADEQUATE — two deterministic defects escaped a green unit suite;
                      pricing row DEFER until the rounding rule is stated
Test basis:           Persona findings (3); unit suite reported green; no requirement IDs supplied
Architecture basis:   stable existing, unverified — no product code in workspace
Quality risks:        1 money correctness (rounding), 2 date/timezone boundary + runtime TZ config,
                      3 control labelling (usability/accessibility)
Manual evaluation:    Persona agents = exploratory evaluation. One charter, time box and evidence
                      record (steps, inputs, timestamps, environment/build ID) per persona; run on
                      the preview candidate before promotion; report only, never gate; findings
                      never count as verified evidence
Adequacy signals:     Escaped-defect analysis: 2 deterministic escapes (oracle/boundary gap);
                      persona findings that have a deterministic oracle should trend to zero;
                      mutation testing on pricing and date logic after the fix
Handoffs:             defect-shift-left (placement of the rounding and boundary tests);
                      ci-cd-reliability-architecture (move persona runs to preview before promotion,
                      non-blocking; TZ smoke check); requirements-grounding (rounding rule,
                      cutoff timezone); UX/accessibility owner (button labels)
Residual risk:        Unknown — root cause of both unit-test passes not inspected
Next action:          Get the rounding rule from the pricing owner, then add the escaped case as a
                      failing regression test
Verification:         Not run — workspace holds no product code or tests
```

Triage rule for all future persona findings: if the finding has a deterministic oracle (wrong amount, wrong date), treat it as an escaped defect and add the test at the earliest stage that can catch it. If it needs judgment (an unclear control), make it an issue for its owner.
